text.p: Belgian steel maker Cockerill Sambre said on Wednesday it was happy with the performance of its Eko Stahl unit in eastern Germany, which made a 1996 loss of 123 million marks after reaching break-even in 1995.

"We are totally satisfied with Eko Stahl. It corresponds exactly to what we expected," Cockerill chairman Jean Gandois told a news conference about the Belgian group's 1996 results. Cockerill bought 60 percent of Eko Stahl in January 1995.
Eko Stahl had no impact on Cockerill's group result, and 100 million marks of the loss was covered by German privatisation authorities, as promised when Cockerill made the purchase.

Cockerill said an ongoing 1.1 billion mark investment plan for the eastern German steel maker was on schedule. A new blast furnace would be set going in April and a new wide-band rolling mill would be officially opened in July.
"From summer, Eko Stahl will have a complete industrial outline...," Cockerill said in a statement.
Eko produced 1.9 million tonnes of liquid steel in 1996.
